sections.churn_summary: Across the five active assessment-model books, guards are aligned (`exit_confirm_screens=2`, `reentry_cooldown_screens=1`, `min_rebalance_notional_gbp=10.0` except `ai_judgment_hold5_fair` at 5 screens), and the latest pass shows no duplicate-day skips, zero adjacent buy/sell flips in the 7-day window, and hold-buffer activity only on the hold-5 twin (`buffer_holds_planned=1`, `buffered_holdings=1`, `last_run.trade_count=0`). Recent churn is quieter than lifetime totals on the primary: `ai_judgment_fair` lifetime `cost_drag=0.1385` and `trade_count=36` (watch alert) versus epoch-scoped `cost_drag=0.0197` and `post_apply_trade_count=26` on the fair-cost epoch, while the control `buy_tier_level` stays low drag at `0.0071` with higher activity (`trade_count=107`, 14 trades in 7d). The 7-day buffered-hold replay for `ai_judgment_fair` and `buy_tier_level` still ties on `trade_count_delta_lower_minus_higher=0` with only `cost_drag_delta_lower_minus_higher=-0.0001`, so screen-count guard tuning is not separating outcomes in this window. The single biggest operational learning gap is that `exit_shadow` reports `closed_count=0` on every active track (e.g. `ai_judgment_fair` `open_count=14`), so post-exit cohorts still cannot inform guard or selectivity decisions despite elevated primary lifetime drag.
